report.source_text: Histopathological examination of the resected tumor revealed a predominantly lepidic growth pattern with mucin secretion under low-power view (Fig. 1C). Middle-power magnification revealed tumor cells with abundant apical cytoplasmic mucin and small, basally oriented nuclei (Fig. 1D). The partial tumor exhibited an invasive pattern of infiltrative glands lined by tumor cells containing abundant intracytoplasmic mucin, measuring less than 5 mm in size (Fig. 1E). Notably, the focal area exhibited atypical goblet cell hyperplasia (Fig. 1F, arrows) in the bronchial epithelium (Fig. 1F, triangles). The resection margin and lymph nodes were negative. The immunohistochemical staining results were as follows: CK7 was positive (Fig. 1G), TTF-1 was negative (Fig. 1H), and CK5/6 staining revealed no evidence of a basal cell layer (Fig. 1I).
